It seemed stupid to think that in time of question that they wouldn’t let her take the test, and then work out the problems later. I told her not to worry and that I would go to the School tomorrow and see what was happening. One can never tell what these Orientals are thinking and how their minds work.

MAR 08

        Was anious anxious for the morning to pass so that I could go to USCAR and the University so as to check why Junko couldn’t take the test. After lunch I caught the Naha bus and went to see Mr. Evans at USCAR. He was sorry to hear of the affair and said I should go to the University and talk to them.

        At the University I saw an American, and upon questioning him, I found him to be one of the Michigan State men, who are assisting in getting this new University on its feet. I told him the story and he took me to an interpreter who in turn took me to the Registrar. After telling him the story, he checked into Junko Kugai’s records. After a few minutes he said that the reason that Junko wasn’t allowed to take the test was that she hadn’t completed the application. It seems that she had thought a teacher friend from Miyako was going to complete the form and he thought she was finish it. Thus, through this unfortunate misunderstanding, the application wasn’t completed and consequently Junko was not eligible to take the entrance exam. I was sorry to hear this, but since she had made the mistake, and not the University, there wasn’t anything that could be done.

        I thanked them all and started for home. On the way the Michigan State man showed me the new library – very nice – and also pointed out the new science building. Physically the new University is shaping up very nicely and soon it will be one of the better ones in the Orient. The big problem is good teachers and they are working on that problem now.

MAR 09

        Junko came to work today and I told her of the unfortunate mistake. Also, tried to emphasize that she had taken part in making the mistake, and she should learn from this mistake that whenever applying for school, a job or whathaveyou, that she should make sure herself that the application is complete. She seemed a little disappointed, but not as bad as she did on Wednesday. The worst thing is that she feels bad about letting down the 3 fellows who chipped in to send her to school.

        Not much else that is new. Completed my estimate on topsoiling and mulching and settled down to finishing up a little personal work. Think I am going to have to put in for a 3 day pass!

        Lyle Nelson – Carol Chervitz’s financé came over in the evening, and ate at the mess hall. Then we saw one of the worst movies that I have ever seen – ”The Return of Jack Slade” – too awful to even think about. We then went to the Castle Terrace and had a couple drinks plus some sandwiches to go with the fine music. Still it is a little rough to sit while others dance, but I really don’t mind it that much. We talked about his trip to Hong Kong – he spent a month in that fine city last January. Also discussed his plans for the future – wedding August 12th, and his going home. It was an enjoyable evening and we will have to do it again some time in the near future.

MAR 10

        Today was the day of the Big Inspection. Colonel Page, the new Acting District Engineer was scheduled to inspect the troops and the barracks this morning. Consequently the maids had gotten the barracks in top top shape, and the boys had cleaned up the area a little bit. At 9:30 in the morning we got in formation and were given “open ranks, march.” Here, and in this position, we stood for a little over ½ hour waiting for the inspecting officer.

        Colonel Page finally showed up, and spent the next ½ hour inspecting the ranks. I must admit that I think he was one of the best inspecting officers that I have stood in formation for. He didn’t ask silly and unnecessary questions, and bothered himself with just the carbines and pistols. And concerning the carbines, he only had good things to say, such as “good bore,” “nice looking weapon,” etc. Upon completition of the inspection we were dismissed to our barracks in order to stand by until he came through the barracks.

        Sam and I were interested in what he was going to say about the bar, and also whether Capt. Schlag and M/Sgt Veomett would attempt to cover it up. Surprising enough, they volunteered to show the Colonel the room, and also surprising, he said he thought it was a good idea and was all for it. His only question was the legality of the bar and asked them to make sure there is nothing wrong about having beer and whiskey in the barracks.

        The Colonel also said that he didn’t see any sense in having foot locker displays, and it was all right with him to do away with it, Sooo, for once, I thought a Colonel acted in common sense and did a creditable job.

MAR 11 (SUNDAY - WEEK 64)

        The old saying is that if it rains on Easter Sunday, that it will rain the next 7 Sundays. Well, here on Okinawa it is the reverse, as it appears to be raining Sundays from now until Easter. I hadn’t seen it rain as hard in many months as it did this morning. The rain came down in bucketfulls and one dared his life if he went outside. Fortunately I didn’t have any business outside, so I stayed in my room.

        Didn’t do much today. Read a little in the morning, and also spent some time separating clothes that I will take with me and those that I plan to send home. Felt a little good about getting ready for leaving the Rock. Won’t be long now –

        Read all afternoon, primarily Chester Bowles’ book, “The New Dimensions of Peace.” It is an excellent book and presents the critical world situation in clear terms. He cites backgrounds to the Russian and Chinese revolutions, plus an analysis of Indias past and present. His main theme is that colonialism is dead, and the sooner America realizes it and backs some of these underdeveloped countries, the better this democratic world will be. Too often we pour billions into mistakes (allies mistakes) such as Indo-China, yet give little to countries such as Burma and Indonesia. It just seems that we are backing the wrong type of men in Asia, – free nations, yet corrupt leaders.

MAR 12

        The temperature dropped quite low in the night time and stayed with us the whole day. Probably didn’t get any lower than 50 yet it seemed like 20 below, especially in the hut at night. Our poor little stove doesn’t put out much heat, and what there is of it doesn’t seem to enter my room. I guess I am just a well bred St. Louisan – that is, a perpetual criper of weather.

        Decided to investigate the possibilities of a 3 day pass and after giving it more thought, I put in for a 3 day pass starting this Wednesday. No sweat at the office – they know I never work – and seemingly little trouble at the Orderly Room. Sooo – if things work out, I will see if I can’t get some things done during these 3 days. I want to check the airlines, the recruiting office concerning what clothes I have to turn in when I leave, and Kadena elementary school so as to get some information for Carolyn. If the weather turns warmer I might even get in a little tennis.

        In the evening I took Chapman to the Castle Terrace for a going-away dinner. The club steak was pretty good and the meal was a relief from the usual mess hall grub. We stuck around the Club for about 4 hours, – drinking, shooting the breeze and in general having a pretty good time. I am sorry to see him go, for Al and Charlie Terry were the 2 fellows I went around with the most on the Rock. Both were intelligent, well rounded fellows that shared the Army crap, jokes, and banter with me. Anyway, I am glad they are able to get back to their wives and children. (Me too – pretty soon!)

MAR 13

        Crazy weather, – yesterday it was cold, today it is warm. I sure hope it stays this way the next 3-5 days so I can get some exercise plus some things done without getting wet. Finished one estimate and did a little work on the latest estimate that I was given. As I have noticed lately, I have been getting requests from Army Branch which are not ready for estimating. This results in my running around and finally tabling the work until everything is done.

        Received a letter from Jeri Lusmd_n_ and Dow Chemical in answer to the letter that I hads had sent him a couple weeks ago. In the letter he said that my job is available when I return whether it be in June or September. Also he said that all the fellows in the Department are making at least $6000/year and most likely I will get at least that much. He also enclosed some pamphlets concerning the work they have been doing lately and said probably I would work in the Rolling Mill setting standard on some of the Mills. (Doesn’t sound interesting at all) One sentence was interesting, he said that if I wasn’t planning to return to Dow that I should let him know. Guess he caught the undertone in the letter, for I have my doubts about returning to Dow unless it be in Production or Labor Relations.

        Must have been the food for I had an upset stomach today, like I had yesterday. Oh well, can’t expect much more from Army chow. Have noticed that lima beans give me indigestion, so will have to eliminate this vegetable. Still the hyopchondrious hypochondriac!

MAR 14

        Signed out right after breakfast and so began my 3 day pass. The weather was great – sunny, yet with a cool breeze. I picked up a jeep around 9:30 and went to Northwest Airlines to get some information concerning flights from here to Cairo. Obtained a little information, but the best feature was that I got a copy of the Airline Guide for February, and will thus be able to try and arrange the trip stopping in the cities that I want to visit.

        In the afternoon I went to the Kadena Elementary School to see if I could get some additional information for Carolyn. Again I talked to the Principal, and as before, I didn’t get much of value to relay home. She didn’t seem too interested in my talking to any of the teachers, so I was sort of stymied. Later in the day I jotted down those things that I think Carolyn might be interested in, and ended the letter saying that she had to make up her own mind.

        Played some tennis later on in the afternoon and had some fine volleys. The day was perfect for tennis and I got some fine exercise for the hour and a quarter that I was on the court. My game is sure off, and I will have to start playing a lot to get back in shape.

MAR 15

        Today wasn’t nearly the day that yesterday had been. It looked as if it was going to rain any minute, consequently, I didn’t go out to the golf course like I planned. Instead I journeyed up to the tennis courts and played a little tennis. However, the wind was extremely strong and made volleying difficult.

        I guess I am on sort of a reading “jog” at the present. Started reading “War and Peace” today and I hope to finish it before I leave here. Also, finished Chester Bowles’s book, and Elmer Davis’s new book, “Two Minutes till Midnight.” This book, like the first one, (C.B.) is the work of a liberal and I tend to go along with the basic ideas. I especially enjoyed Bowles’s book, and agree wholeheartedly with his thoughts that the main thing we have to offer to the world is not our material wealth, but our democratic principles of equality, liberty, freedom, etc. It is remarkable how these things are now taken for granted ,and the main thing the American populace talks about is the material gains that he has.

        Read Factory Magazine and a booklet concerning American foreign policy in 1954. Also glanced through some insurance articles that Jerome had sent me. Soooo – at least I am making good use of my time. (Today anyway!)

MAR 16

        The weather looked bad, when I gazed out the window at 6:15 AM, and consequently I decided to wait before going out to play golf. Read in the morning, and again the afternoon as it proceded to pour bucketfulls of rain. At some intervals one could hardly see out the window the rain was coming down so hard. Am continuing on my War and Peace project, and it is sure slow headway. Oh well, as the ER or draftee says, “I’ve nothing but time!”

        Went to Naha in the evening and saw 2 lousy movies at the Kahuli Ko Kahuli Kan movie theater. (Also, it costs 70 ¥ to get in the balcony, an inflated price if I ever paid one) one of the movies was shots of a strip show in Mexico. The women wore next to nothing and I am not exaggerating. There were 4 strippers and each of them ended their act with nothing on but triangular G-strings and half dollar covers. The bumps, grinds and motions they did on the screen were something I have never seen in the movies. To say the least, I have am sure such a movie could not be shown on U.S. screens, except at stag parties. (I wonder what the Oriental thinks of when he sees such a movie?)

MAR 17

        For a change the sun came out, and we figured it would be out only during training and then go underneath some clouds in the afternoon. However, we were wrong, as “Old Man Sun” blazed all day. We felt it in the morning as we had 40 minutes of drilling in our OD’s. Also had Character Guidance with that stupid but well meaning – Chaplin at the helm. I worked a pretty good deal this morning; – bought 2 papers and when the character lecture began, I headed for the men’s room in thiis way I missed over ½ of the talk. (Thank Goodness!)

        Reserved a court in the afternoon and went there at 1 PM to get some practice banging the ball against the backboard. About 15 minutes after I had begun, another fellow asked if I would join them in a doubles match (they would use my court). I gladly said yes as the 3 players were in the top 5 or 6 on the Island.

        We played 2 sets, and my inexperience was the difference as we lost both of them by scores of 603, 705. However, I played better than usual, and really enjoyed myself throughout the two sets. The men were quite cool, and played my backhand perfectly, that is, to get points for themselves. Also, one of the fellows looking on, said he would help me with my backhand, so, it was an enjoyable afternoon.

MAR 18 (SUNDAY - WEEK 65)

        Arranged to go to Kin Village if the weather was half-way decent. After breakfast the sky was a little dark but Ken Lichius and I decided to take a chance and go anyway. We left around 9:30 and went by bus to Ishikawa where we managed to get a ride to Kin.

        The weather was pretty good for picture taking and I took about 22 shots of interesting sights in and around the village. Kin is a somewhat prosperous village with well lays laid out streets, and particularly the washing facilities. In one section of the village there are two concrete structures, one for obtaining water from the a spring flowing from a hill, and the other one for washing clothes. The washing area was crowded with women and i took a couple pictures of the women at work.

        Near this area is located a rice polishing plant. We walked in and around the building and watched the men and machines busy at work. The equipment is quite crude and the output low, but I guess the people produce enough for their needs and the needs of some of their neighbors. We tried to coax some children to pose for our cameras but got nothing but giggles and glimpses of running children. These people are really camera shy, and all one has to do is put them in a gallop is to raise the camera to eye level.

        From here we walked towards the beach, and on the way we passed a huge rice paddy area, in which were located many small plots which we presumed belonged to various families in the village. Most of the paddies were under water, and the people in the fields were sloshing in the __een in an effort to cultivate the soil. Some of the people were beginning to transplant the rice stalks in the paddies from the seedling plots that they have been cultivating for a couple of months.

        I was a tired man when I reached the beach and I was glad to sit down on a huge rock and rest awhile. The beach is about the best I have seen on The Rock and for a few minutes I debated about stripping to my undershorts and going in for a swim. However, it began to get cool and I decided against it. The beach is composed of fine sand and stretches for a mile or so. The water seemed to be deep enough for swimming yet not too deep that one is a little skeptical of going out.

        AFter awhile we headed back and walked among the rice paddies on the way back to the road. Had to keep awake so as not to fall in, but we were able to keep our feet dry. I was a tired man when I returned to Kue, but enjoyed the day quite a bit.

MAR 19

        My 5 days – so to speak – of freedom came to an end and I returned to work. Actually didn’t have too much to do, so I continued reading from the book on plumbing that I checked out from the library. It is a pretty illustrative book and I think it has familiarized me with some of the plumbing terms. Talked to Joe Alfonsi and we sort of decided that it would be best for me to go in person to Formosa to buy the airplane ticket.

        In the evening Adams and I went to our bosses house (Mr. Hands) where we showed our respective slides. It was an interesting – although somewhat tiring – evening. One highlight was the use of Mr. hand’s automatic viewer. It is really some piece of equipment.

MAR 20

        Decided to check on a few things in the afternoon and consequently checked out a jeep at the motor pool. First I went to the Post Office where I air mailed my slides of India home. The cost was $1.60 and I think I have spent a fortune for stamps for various and sundry things since I have been overseas. Next I went to Rycom headquarters where I inquired of certain things concerning my discharge over here. I found out that I would not be able to get any flights once I am discharged. Then I was told that most likely I will only get $100 of separation pay. Concerning my baggage, I was told that I might be able to send one footlocker but would have to have it stated on my orders.

        From here (Rycom) I drove to Sukiran to watch the work for the mooring facilities for the SS Jacona – a floating powerplant soon to be connected in with the electrical distribution system on the island. Not much could be seen so I left soon after I arrived. I am currently working on an estimate for the mooring facilities and had hoped I would be able to learn something of the progress thus far.

        The evening passed soon enough – with nothing in particular being done. Went to the library and read some magazines and then returned to the hut where I read some literature Jerome Barker had sent. Was interested in articles of his company and their Planned Estates Plan, however I don’t think I am too fascinated with the Insurance business or similar sales work. I like the idea of compensation for effort, but right now I am too idealistic and feel money isn’t the main incentive, and that would be the main reason for me to enter the insurance field.

MAR 21

        I don’t know why but this week is sure passing slowly. Seems as if every day I stop to think if this is Friday and then am horrified when I realize it is only Tuesday or Wednesday. Not much doing at work, and for that matter, not much doing on the Island. We changed into our khakis today and I am hoping that I will never have to wear the awful O.D’s again.

        Spent most of the evening reading, both the St. Louis Post Dispatch and War and Peace. The latter book is great and I find it extremely interesting at times. However, I think the tremendous length of the book wears on my mind and I sort of hate to put aside everything else so that I can read the book. Maybe, I will finish it by the time I leave the Rock.

MAR 22

        Nothing new at work and nothing particularly new to write about. Had the afternoon off and decided to play some tennis. I had called one fellow on the “tennis ladder” concerning playing a match but he said he would have to forfeit. This advanced me from 26 to 22. At the courts I happened to find out that number 18 was present so I challenged him. It was a windy and sloppy game, but I managed to win 7-5, 6-3 which boosted me to the Number 18 slot. Don’t really care about my standing except that I will be able to play better people if I am higher up on the ladder.

        In the evening i took in a movie at the Plaza Theater and then stopped in at the Top 3 Club. Did some dancing, and was pleased that I had enough confidence or foolhardiness to dance some “slow” fast steps. Maybe – just maybe – I will someday be able to dance fast.

MAR 23

        How repetitive the days are - it seems that each day is the same as the one before it and most likely the one coming up. Finished a small estimate and spent the rest of the day on various projects, one of which consisted of coping invoice figures in my pricing notebook.

        Went to work in the evening and caught up on some of my typing. Wrote to D_n, Mom, Uncle Jerome and answered an ad to the Pillsbury people about an Industrial Relations Trainee job. Jerome had sent me some pamphlets about Insurance and also asked me if I was interested in working for the Home Life Insurance Company. Actually, I am not too enthralled with Insurance, and feel that it as a job with one main goal – money. I guess I am still too idealistic (and perhaps a man of no responsibilities) but feel that is not enough.

        Received a letter from Mom today in which she sent $25 to buy some silk, ivory statues, a table cloth and a couple of other small items. I am glad that she sent the list for I can now shop for the goods and feel that I am getting something that she wants. In this way I can get them some momentos, and yet concentrate on certain things so that I don’t spend all my time shopping, – which I don’t enjoy too much.

MAR 24

        Training runs in cycles and today was no exception. We had an “assault” problem, typical of the training we have been having the past month or two. After a briefing we divided into two squads, one of which was supposed to be mine. After a brief march to the area near the Castle Terrace, we set off for our “jumping off spot”, about 300 yards from an objective – a barren hill top adjacent to the Terrace.

        They had rounded up a couple of walky talkies and thus our problem was a little more realistic. The objective was to get as close to the hill as possible without being seen. To do this we had decided to go as one group until we came to a split in a ravine, from which the two squads would split and continue alone. The first problem was to get to the junction, and we couldn't decide to creep along the sides of the hills or to go to the valley below. We decided on the valley and I doubt that that was the best choice. The grass was from 6’ – 15’ and there were few paths in the first part. We had to push our way through and under the grass, all the time keeping a watch for any habus – this was their season – and to keep from falling in any holes.

        Well after briar stings, and slashes of the grass we finally came upon some rice paddies where we were able to follow some beaten paths. We circled the hill in question and "slashed" and crawled up the hill surprising the observers who had been watching the opposite direction.

Can't say that I really enjoy these exercises although they sure beat Character Guidance lectures and 4 hours of Army films. Give me a couple more weeks of these and I will probably be saying just the opposite.

MAR 25 (SUNDAY - WEEK 66)

        Yesterday I signed up for a court, and so around 9:30 I went to the tennis courts for an hour and a half of tennis. It threatened to rain at any moment but outside of a couple of drops I was able to get my fill of tennis for the day.

The rest of the day was taken up by reading, – all of it on War and Peace. The book is quite interesting and I enjoy it very much. To say the least, it is the longest book that I have ever read and I wonder if I will even finish it. Would like to finish it this week if possible as I would like to start my the planning of my trip in more detail, and also to read a couple of other books and pamphlets that I have on my desk.

Was in Jagaru in the evening and it was interesting to see the Okinawans in their homes at night. Some were eating, others playing the samisen, some walking or shopping and the rest just sitting. Many people that live in Jugaru work in Kue or Sukiran and consequently the this small village in the hills is very crowded. Every available spot seems to be filled by a house, and there are very few that have any kind of a yard in which the kids could play.

        Most of the people were in Western Type dress although there were a few in kimonos or robes. I doubt if this is a very rich village which may be the reason for the absence of kimonos. One does see most of the old women in some kind of a robe or komodos. These women are interesting with their long gray hair tied in a knot in the back, and their tattooed knuckles.

MAR 26

        Another week – 9 to go. Visited some current construction projects in the afternoon and enjoyed observing the construction going on. Such visits help me considerably in my estimating as I have quite a poor background in this type of work. At the Hangar I observed the reinforcing being put in place, the excavation, and foundation being poured. This is one of the simpler projects and afforded me a good project to observe. From here we (Bob Stavely and I) went to the new swimming pool and training center. Both projects are huge and are just about ready to turn over to the Post Engineers.

        Although I had decided not to go to any more Jewish services I decided to give it one more chance. (Who’s giving who a chance?) I made reservations at the Passover Sedar and went there about 7 PM. There were quite a few people at the Mess Hall – Kadena – and I was surprised at the turnout. The service was performed by the young Rabbi who I don’t think too much of, and I was bored through-out the evening. Naturally the fact that much of the service was in hebrew didn’t help any. Perhaps the only redeeming factor was that I met a couple people at the service that I had not seen in some time. Jewish food was served but I didn’t eat very much as I had already eaten in the mess hall. Did enjoy eating matzos though.

MAR 27                FIRST DAY OF PASSOVER

        Felt hypocritical even thinking about going to services so I decided to work. Was given an estimate in the morning concerning manproof grill structures (security fences) and I spent the day working up estimates on them. Really wasn’t much to the estimate once I figured out the blueprint, and so I thought I would play tennis at 4. Old man weather was two steps ahead of me though, and about 3:30 it began to rain which lasted about an hour. Soo I had to content myself with reading the electrical handbook that I checked out of the library.

        Can’t say it was a boring evening, yet it wasn’t a real exciting one. Spent the whole evening reading War and peace and I now am about 70% completed. Maybe with luck I will finish it this week. Took time out to get a hamburger at The Chinaman’s Restaurant and also to have a last sandwich with Schellentrager. One by one the guys are leaving and pretty soon the Engineers will have been whittled down to nothing.

MAR 28

        Another day – another dollar – and one less day in the Army. They didn’t have any estimates to do at work so I just killed the day doing odd things, personal work, and just getting lost.

        Received no mail today, nor had anything unusual occur. Went to the movies in the evening and saw a pretty good Dean Martin and Jerry Lewis movie. One thing for sure and that is I saw some mighty good looking women in the picture. After the show I went to the Castle Terrace for a couple of beers. The boys with whom I went have the slot machine craze and generally play almost every night. Tonight I decided to invest $1 worth and see what I could do. Was lucky and hit a jackpot so I came out $5.50 ahead. Actually was $6.50 ahead at one time, but couldn’t stop, and was only able to drag myself away when I got to the $5.50 mark. The big thing about slot machines is to drag yourself away while you are ahead; – and that is harder to do then it sounds.

MAR 29

        Today was the best of the year – at least with respect to the weather. The sun came out early in the day and stayed out all day, with an occasional hiding behind some clouds. Ate lunch at the Terrace in honor of Mrs. Gay and Mrs. Willard who are soon to depart for the U.S. The meal was excellent and well worth the $.85 that it cost. Both of the ladies received some Siamese silverware as going away presents.

        Payday was today and it was good to get some needed cash in my pocket and then in the bank. This was the first time that I received my 6 year longevity pay and the extra $20 came in handy. Am trying to build up a little reserve for my trip.

        In the afternoon I challenged Paul Fichter to a tennis match in the ladder tournament and it turned out to be a lulu. I won the first one 6-2, he then took the second set 9-7 and we then began the 3rd and final set. I then got lucky and took the first 5 games of the 3rd set only to see him take 3 straight games and I thought it would be a repeat of the 2nd set. However I took the next game and so ended the match. Thus, I now am now 14th and maybe I will be able to play some good players.

        Read War and Peace for 4 hours in the evening.

MAR 30

        Again no work and so I didn’t do much today. In the afternoon they go gave me an informed estimate to do and I passed the time working on it. Took off for Machinato around 2 PM and talked to a few firms concerning boat rides to Hong Kong, and from Hong Kong to Port Said, Egypt. The cheapest fare is $319 and so it seems that flying – if I get ⅓ off – would be the best bet; that is, unless I work my way home on a ship.

        I talked to Ted Sjobery who had been in the Merchant Marine (like Morton) and said that it might be possible to get a job on a foreign ship. Probably my best bet would be to fly to Hong Kong and inquire there about getting a job. However, I have my doubts concerning this latter way of going home.

        Went to the movies in the evening and then to the Top 3 club. Had a few drinks, talked to a Sgt that I knew and headed home.

        

MAR 31

        We thought that we wouldn’t have any training this morning on account of tomorrow being Easter, but we were quite surprised. Training consisted of 3 training films and I don’t believe I have ever seen 3 duller movies. At the finish of the 1st movie I went to my hut and “bugged out” during most of the second film. After we finished the 3rd films we had physical training which consisted of a couple games of volleyball. This was the first volleyball game that we have played in a long time and I enjoyed the games.

        In the afternoon I happened to talk to Veomett (1st Sgt) and he mentioned that they had an opening in their golf foursome that was to drive off at 1:30. I said that I would like to play – first time since August – and Davy Hurst and I took a taxi to the golf course. I rented clubs and paid the greens fee (sand greens) and we were soon on our way. Didn’t do too bad the first couple of holes but on the 5th I blasted two into the “boondocks.” This busted my game wide open and soon I was playing my same old game. Putting gave me a lot of trouble and I couldn’t judge how to hit on sand greens. Don’t know what my score way was, but I doubt if I broke 100. Enjoyed the game and exercise, though.

APR 01 (SUNDAY - WEEK 67)                 EASTER SUNDAY

        In one sense I wanted it to rain today since I had a lot of reading planned; but on the other hand I didn’t want to ruin it for the other fellows. Well, – it rained in the morning (typical Okinawan Sunday) and so I stayed in the hut and finished War and Peace. It was a struggle but I am glad I started and finished the book, for it is one of the better books that I have read.

        Started to read again in the afternoon, but Sam yelled in that they were getting up a volleyball game. Trotted out to the court, and for the next 2 ½ hours we batted the ball and fought the wind. Many times the wind caught the ball and either stopped it or had it sailed on out of bounds. Enjoyed the exercise and I am sure my wrists will be sore tomorrow morning.

        Went to Jagaru Village in the evening and had a drink in the Smile Bar. While I was in the bar a loud mouthed GI – half plastered – threatened the bar tendy and demanded a beer to replace the beer in the bottom of his glass that he said the ball bar tender threw out. One of his the G.I’s friends got up and tried to quiet him down, and I thought I would throw in a few words and suggest that he pay for the beer that he intimidated from the Okinawan. Right A away I realized my mistake, for the guy got all hopped up and asked me if I wanted to fight. Well, I decided to say no more and talked to the girl who had brought my drink. About 20 minutes later I left and thought the guy would come out and start trouble – but he didn’t. Anyway it proves that I ought to keep quiet and not get mixed up with drunks, unless I am looking for trouble.

APR 02

        Thought that there would be some work today but still no requests came in for estimates. So I read from the electrical handbook that I have and also did a little personal work. In the afternoon I went to a party at the Castle Terrace in honor of the new District Engineer. The party was really crowded and it was a little difficult to get some of the free drinks and sandwiches floating around. Managed to get my share though and had a fine time ignoring the Colonel and talking to the boys. Around 5:45 I left and had chow at the mess hall.

        Not much doing in the evening. Finished reading The Man in the Gray Flannel Suit which was a fair book but nothing to shout about. Sorry that the Chinaman’s Restaurant closes at 7:30 for I could have used a cup of coffee and was to lazy to go to the club. Finally hit the sack around 11 PM.

        One of the major problems that I have been thinking about stared me in the face today; that is, “Should I associate with everyone and have no real good friends, or should I join a clique and have 7 or 8 close friends. Up to now I have leaned towards the former, trying to be friends with all, since this is such a small, closely packed unit and we are all here not of our own free choosing. Consequently, I drift back and forth among the groups that have evolved spending some time with the quiet bunch and other evenings with the “good __es” or heavy drinkers. Before when Chapman, Terry and some of the others were here, we use to have some good intellectual conversations, but the quiet ones that have replaced them are not of the same breed. Probably, if men like Doe, Manse Hall, etc were here I would be inclined to spend more time with them.

        On the other hand, the more noisy boys and the heavy drinkers are more numerous and in some respects are quite decent fellows. Some of them are friendly and I get along with them even though I am not familiar with all their conversations since I do not hang around with them. Some of these guys are “nothing” and quite childish. Howe I am sure I would never go out of my way to make more than a passing acquaintance with them in civilian life. It is some of these latter fellows that sort of resent my shifting from clique to clique and see it to be an encroachment on their little groups with which they feel secure and which they have fomented, at the sacrifice to the unit, these small groups.

        Quite a problem, although I might be making more of it then there actually is. This would not be true as much in civilian life where you do not live, eat and work with the same fellows day in and day out. Still it is questions such as this and also my future work that I would like to give much thought to and perhaps come to some decision while I am in the Army and have free time.

APR 03

        Things must be slow with the District for again today no requests for estimates came in to our section. Consequently I did odd things all day; just trying to pass the time. In the morning I gave Junko some money and told her to go to the American clinic and have them determine what the rash was on her face. She came back about 20 minutes later and said that they wanted to see me at the clinic. I went there and they told me she has the measles! Great, but I am hoping that my having them before will prevent me from catching them now.

APR 04

        Junko didn’t show up today – naturally, and consequently I had to make my own bed. This is the first time in many months and I didn’t put much effort into it. I think I made it in the same as I use to back home, – that is, to pull back the covers and to tuck in loose ends here and there.

        Finally a request for an estimate came in and was assigned to me. It is a “red ball” (rush job), however I have about 8 days to work on it. It concerns relocation of an artillery unit on account of the extension of the runway at Kadena. I don’t think it will require much work, though.

        About 4:50 PM I received a phone call from the Colonel who I had called concerning a challenge match on the ladder tournament. He said that he could play this afternoon and I said that I would meet him at the Kue courts at 5:15. The weather was pretty nice and we had a good 2 sets, from which I emerged a 6-4, 6-3 victor. Consequently I move up to 10 on the tennis ladder. I am afraid that this will be short lived as there are some decent players in slots behind me. One thing I am sorry about is that I don’t think my playing has improved very much, and I have only been winning because the opponents haven’t been good.

APR 05

        Again I made my bed and put out my blankets and mattress to air. Sure hope Junko comes back soon as I don’t like these additional duties. Heard from one of the maids that her measles are the short term kind and that she would probably be back on Friday.

        The day was beautiful and I was glad today was our “organized athletics day.” I signed up for a court and volleyed with Paul for awhile in an effort to try out my racket that I had fixed. The handle is bigger that than the supply room one that I have been using, and I don’t like it as well. One of the players, – No. 12 – challenged me to a match which took up the next 1 ¾ hours. He emerged victorious 6-8, 6-4, 6-4 in what I considered a lousy match although I give him credit for the final win. Would like to put the blame on the heavier racket, but it was just my poor playing. Anyway, I didn’t drop too far, plus the exercise was good. Can’t say that I enjoyed the game though.

        Stayed home in the evening and finished the book i was reading – The American Lawyer. It was a fair book and answers some of my questions concerning the legal profession.

APR 06

        Junko came back today and consequently I returned to my life of leisure. No more bed making unless I leave the Army – at least that is a paradox if nothing else is! Seems like I spent the day worrying about her. In the afternoon Sgt. Woodson and I went to see Kinjo concerning the possibility of her getting a job as a clerk-typist. He said that things were tight and that they weren’t hiring anyone at the present. I then talked to the typing pool boss and Air Force Construction, but nothing available in either place. Finally decided to ask Mr. Hands, and he said that while he needed more typists, he couldn’t hire anyone until he got the word from above.

        Back to my desk to do some estimating and to give more thought to the problem. Decided that since Junko had spare time, perhaps she could work in our office in the afternoon, doing productive work and at the same time getting needed practical experience on her part. I would continue to pay her as a maid, for she wouldn’t get anything from OKED. Besides the experience, if something opened up, she would be the logical person to fit into the picture. I spoke to Mr. Hands and he said he was O.K. with him, and Sophia said he was all right with her, so all I need now is Junko’s approval.

        Went to Naha in the evening and saw the movie The Student Prince. Also bought a record of China Night, something to remind me of the Orient!

APR 07

        Another inspection by the District Engineer, this time by Colonel Finley who just recently took over the job with the Okinawa Engineer District. Naturally the panic button was pushed and we had our customary pep talk, “police call” and other harassment that comes with inspections. At 8:45 we fell out and stood in “Open Ranks” until approximately 9:31 AM when Colonel Finley came on the scene. Attention was given and he proceded to inspect the troops. He walked so fast that we were almost unable to get our womens weapons to inspection arms. I think he reviewed the whole works in no more than 4 minutes and didn’t spend much more than 10 minutes in the company area. So goes the Army and the panic that accompanies it.

        Played volleyball in the evening afternoon and enjoyed the games. Unlike last summer there isn’t any arguing or yelling and things are pretty good and humorous. Around 4 PM I went to Jagaru to finish the roll of film that I have had in my camera since I was in Bangkok. I hope this long interval of time didn’t spoil any of the pictures

        Went to the movies in the evening and saw “Good Morning Miss Dove.” It was a good movie and reminded me of Miss Bru_ns, – the one and only Miss Bru_ns! Read part of the Post-Dispatch and then spent an hour or so at the Club. Back to 722 and to bed.

APR 08 (SUNDAY - WEEK 68)

        It rained during the night so I didn’t play tennis as I had planned. Instead I did some reading and now I have pretty well caught up on my reading backlog and now I will try and concentrate on my proposed trip. The first thing on the agenda is whether I should fly, take a boat or to try and work my passage. I think I will go to Formosa at the end of the month and see if I can get the ticket at a discount and if so, I will probably fly as far as Cairo.

        In the afternoon I joined Stavely, Lichius and Oats on a sight-seeing tour of Naha. We went to the area near the Teahouse of the August Moon, which besides being a night club area, is the location of the famous Naha Shrine where prayers are asked for departing persons. Today happened to be the birthday of the Buddha, and consequently they had some dancing, singing, puppet shows etc at the Buddhist Temple near the Shrine. We watched the show for a while and also the many people that had come to see the performers. (Mainly Okinawan girl scouts).

        From here we walked to Naha proper and had a bottle of pop. Caught a bus back to Kue around 4:15 as it began to rain making sight-seeing an unpleasant task. Have to comment on all the building going on in Naha. To be sure it is not like Delhi or the states, but still everywhere one looks, new houses (all wooden) stores (reinforced concrete) and misc street improvements are being completed. Naha has plenty of space to expand, and if the economy can support such a huge city, I wouldn’t be surprised if Naha doubles in size in the near future. It is interesting to witness this birth of an erand_y from war destruction.

APR 09

        Spent the day in the office getting caught up on my Kadena estimate. Have to complete it soon, as it is due Thursday. However I don’t anticipate any trouble finishing it on time.

        Came back to the hut around 5:30 and watched Sam and Larson show their new slides with Sam’s new projector. After the slides were shown, we sat around, telling jokes, stories, and tales for about 3 ½ hours. Finally broke up around 9:30 and I took a bath and settled down to reading Time magazine. Didn’t progress very far when Sam yelled in and said that the “Bar” was open and for me to shake a leg. Sooo I put down the magazine and had a couple of scotch and waters with Sam and Copeland.

        More shop talk continued for the next ½ hours and thus my evening passed. Copeland – a pretty decent RA Master Sgt. – said that he had gotten word that the 8105th was soon to be absorbed by Rycom. This would probably mean that the “great deal” we have at Kue would be eliminated. I am sorry to hear this not for me because I will probably be gone, for the sake of those that are presently in the unit and those that ars are coming in the future.

        Kue truly was fate at its best. The job turned out to be pretty good, the billets top (3 men in private rooms plus a bar) (SGT’S HUT), maids, mess hall girls, access to the Castle Terrace, and a minimum of harassment. Everyone who visits Kue is amazed at what we are fortunate to have here. Still we gribe, but I must admit that we do it with tongue in cheek.

APR 10

        Not much new at the office today. Brought Junko to the office in the afternoon and introduced her to Sophie and Helen. As we had discussed Friday, she was going to work every afternoon, and in this manner she would be able to acquire needed typing experience. She wouldn’t get paid for it, as I will continue to pay her as a maid, but I think she will be able to help the section plus doing herself a lot of good.

        At the end of the afternoon Sophie remarked that she was a good typist and would work out fine. Junko told me that she enjoyed the afternoon a lot and liked doing the work. Also, she said that everybody was extremely kind to her. I am glad things seem to be working out so well.

        Applied for a leave today which will go in effect on April 25th. I plan to go to Taiwan to get my plane ticket and then up to japan for some sightseeing and in order to get some visas. Went to CAT and obtained some travel information concerning flights and visas. The lady loaned me an airplane guide and I explored through it in the evening. Was lucky to find a flight that goes to the places that I plan to visit and so things seem pretty good. Now the next big thing is to get a good exchange price for my dollars in Taiwan.

APR 11

        Typical working day, nothing unusual happening while putting in my time in room 136, – the Construction Service Branch. Junko worked again this afternoon and seems to like the work. I hope a job opportunity becomes available to her.

        Went to Naha in the evening amidst takusan rain. Saw Fantasia at the local theater and enjoyed the movie very much. Walt Disney was sure 5-10 years ahead of his time when he made this picture back in 1950. I saw it at that time, but must admit that I didn’t appreciate or enjoy it at that time.

        Since I have been in the Army I have become quite interested in classical music and I plan to increase our collection at home. Perhaps if possible I will buy or even build a Hi Fi set. Can’t say that I really understand the music, but I find it pleasing, and restful. Tchaikovsky is my favorite, particularly some of his catchy stanzas in his works. Might even consider a music appreciation course.

APR 12

        Didn’t realize when I read George Orwell’s 1984 that someday I would be experiencing the same thing. But today it happened – we were told to repoch report to the Day Room at 1:30 in order to listen to a radio broadcast by General White. Yes, “Big Brother” was talking to the lovely proletariat about personal conduct and our actions in time of war. Sorry to say that I wasn’t very interested, and dozed off and on during the twenty minute program. (Just 7 more weeks of this crap!)

        Today was organized athletics but the weather didn’t cooperate. Andy and I joked with the maids in his hut for about a half hour before I decided to go to the PX and then to the library. Around 4 PM I went to the tennis court and practiced hitting the ball against the backboard.

        Saw Kecho while playing tennis and asked her to the show in the evening. Met her at 7 in front of the movie theater, and saw a lousy movie. Walked her back to her compound where we sat and talked awhile. She had been a maid for a couple of years and could speak good English. I was interested in her relationship with her employers as they took her with them where ever they went, – whether it was to a movie, to the Castle Terrace, or to a friends house for dinner. She lived at the house and really liked the couple. Needless to say she was disappointed when they left. – Somewhat of an interesting evening.

APR 13

        The day started off with a bang – Captain Ugis inspected the troops at reveille. Frankly he sickens my stomach and my opinion of what West Point does to me is lowered everytime he talks, walks and acts. He acts so prissy and exacting, yet is no fine example of how to dress and act. His remarks concern how to stand, how the hands should be at the seams, the tilt of the hat, etc. I had to laugh at his remarks to Sjoberg about standing up straight, for Ted is 29 and had served 4 years as a Cadet Midshipman and hates the Army and Captain Ugis.

        Worked on a big estimate today which will probably last a week or so as it is quite complicated. The estimate concerns POL system and J-sets at Ya_take and the difficulty of getting to the job site adds to the d time consuming estimate.

        Didn’t do much in the evening. Read a small book I had, concerning japan, which I found to be so-so. Also, spent a little time on my tour. Getting close! First on the list is Formosa and Japan, so I have been reading up on them lately. Actually, there is a dearth of information of former, however, I don’t plan to stay there long.

APR 14

        Didn’t do much in training today. The CO was not in the area so the main object was to get “lost” for a couple of hours. I was designated as a squad leader and consequently I led my squad to a hill-top near the Castle Terrace and stayed there for a couple of hours. Around 10:30 we came back to the company area and adjourned to the huts.

        In the evening Bob Stavely and I saw The Desperate Hours at the Mercy theater. It was a fine movie and kept my attention through-out the picture. Humphrey Bogart like Frank Sinatra, is one of the top actors in Hollywood today.

        After the movie we went to naha where we headed for the All Club. The girl at the door ushered us into a semi-private room, where we found the typical low table and a couple of pillows to sit on. A Okinawan naisan came in and brought some hot sake. She joined our growing, little party, and soon another girl came in. Both of them were dressed in kimonos and attempted to amuse us, plus pour our drinks.

        Neither of the girls were particularly pretty, nor did they have pretty kimonos. We talked to them and played their little match games for the 2 hours that we were there. During this time other girls came in, sized us up and talked to us for awhile. None of the girls were as pretty as the ones that were in our party the last time we were here. At 11 PM we told them that we weren’t staying for the night and got a quick brush off. Oh well, it was an interesting evening.

APR 15 (SUNDAY - WEEK 69)

        Unbelievable – today was an extremely brilliant day. The sun came out early in the morning and blazed down from a cloudless night sky. I played tennis in the morning and it felt good to have the sun beating down and the sweat pouring from the pores.

        In the afternoon I took my swim suit and journeyed to Kadena where I met Junko. I had promise to take her swimming and luckily it turned out to be a fine day for it. We boarded the bus and went to a beach near the town of Alfuso. Ken Lichius was on the bus and we asked him to join us. He did, although he was interested in taking pictures and not swimming.

        The beach was quite nice and there were about 50 people swimming and/or eating a picnic dinners. The water looked good so we dashed into the water only to find it extremely shallow as the tide was out. Further out we could see a coral reef and decided to go there hoping for deeper water.

        The ordeal getting to the reef and returning was one of the worst that I have encountered in many a year. The ocean bottom was loaded with sea urchins with sharp quills on their backs. There were literally millions of these devils and one almost had to pick his way among the small, brown colored urchins. Then, as if that they weren’t wasn’t enough, the coral reef did much damage to my Americano-sensitive feet. Every few minutes I was yelling, cursing or muttering to myself as I stepped on some sharp object.

        We finally got to the reef, but it looked so lousy that we decided to turn back. At times I just wished to stay here the rest of my life instead of fighting the urchins and coral.

        Consequently, for the 2 hours or so we were in the water we did relatively little swimming. I got many cuts and bruises and longed for my tennis shoes or some other shoes.

        The only salvation was the seashore objects we saw. Besides the urchins there were small crabs, blow fish, five armed star fish, long, black, weird looking objects and blue objects which looked like star fish but appeared dead. Near the shore there were land crabs, small fish and many beautiful sea shells. Junko pointed out some sea food (weed) that her people ate and some little creatures that were supposed to have minor stings.

        Around 5 we gathered our things together and headed for home. My feet keep me from saying I had an enjoyable time.

APR 16

        Didn’t do much during the day. Worked on a big estimate and tried to figure out the piping by myself. Decided in the end to get help, but only to ascertain what I had estimated and to see if I left out anything. Fig_uara, a Japanese Engineer, helped me and together we finished this section of the estimate. I have picked up a lot concerning plumbing, while on the other hand, I haven’t done very well with electricity.

        Lyle came over in the evening and we went to Castle Terrace. Enjoyed being with him and discussing things in common. He leaves on the 27th (maybe sooner) and will have been in the Far East over 18 months. I think his wedding is set for August 12th

APR 17

        Not much new today. Worked on the big estimate that I have been spending my time on lately, and I guess I have am making a little progress on the project. There are also requests for estimates for projects on Okino and Miyako and thus Delmundo and Fig_uara will probably assist me on the estimate.

        Received my orders, and checked immediately with Mrs. Misgen about transportation facilities. I decided to move up my departure to taiwan till Monday as I might have some difficulty in getting a hop back to Okinawa. I will probably spend 3 days on Formosa and do some sightseeing plus seeing about getting my airplane ticket.

        Received a letter from Al Dore in the morning and he says that he will be here on the 29th and 30th with the Air Force Band. I will probably postpone my trip to Japan until after the 30th so I can see him. Actually, a couple days later won’t make any difference at all.

        Spent the evening reading Time, the editorial page of the post and a couple travel books that I have. It is about time for me to start concentrating a little bit more on my trip, if I am going to get anything out of it.

APR 18

        Hard to write much about this day, other to say that it was a typically ordinary day. Went to the new Sukiran PX in the afternoon and priced some items – Didn’t have enough money to buy perfume for Morton but will do so in the next week or so. The PX is quite nice and has many articles for sale, and all of them are displayed on modern counters and displays. Far cry from the PX’s I knew in Pusan, although the Hialeah PX wasn’t too bad.

        Went to the movies in the evening and saw The Tender Trap with Frank Sinatra. The movie was great and I thoroughly enjoyed it. Old Sinatra has a magic touch, for it seems that every movie that he is in is quite good.

        After the movie, Sam, Copeland (M/Sgt who lives in our hut and who is quite decent – for a RA) adjourned to Hut 722 bar for a couple drinks. The bar comes in handy and provides an inexpensive means of passing the evening. Sam is awaiting travel orders home and is quite anxious to leave the Rock, – and I guess for that matter, who isn’t?

APR 19

        Had somewhat of a hectic day today. Had a drivers training course in the morning, after which I returned to the section to work on the FEC 703 estimate. Today was my afternoon off for organized athletics and I told a couple of the waitresses that I would teach them how to play tennis in the middle of the afternoon.

        I dressed and about 1:30 I gathered my stuff together and made ready to leave for the courts. All of a sudden, Sam burst into the hut and he said his plane was leaving within the hour and asked if I would pack his duffle back while he got his medical check. I quickly entered his room and dumped his belongings in the duffle and handbag. He returned about 1:45 and I drove him to the Administration Building, where he got final clearance. From here we drove to the Kadena Airport.

        We arrived just in time and he was able to book on the flight headed for California and the U.S. So ends his tenure on The Rock and now, back to civilization America style.

        In the evening I went to a movie at The Plaza and saw a real tear-jerker. After the movie I went to the Club Top 3 and did more dancing than I have done in many a moon. Am beginning to attempt fast dancing and I find that I like it even though I am not too good. There wasn’t very many people at the club tonight, perhaps it is getting too close to the end of the month.

APR 20

        Finally completed the 703 estimate that I have spent so much time on lately. Cleared up some other matters around the office and prepared to leave on my brief visit to Taiwan beginning Monday. Received money in the mail from mom and bought travellers checks with it. I will also take along some greenbacks in case I am able to get a better trade-in value with them.

        Around 7:30 I heard a noise at the window and went to investigate. It turned out to be an Okinawan boy whom I had met at work. He was interested in conversing with an American so as to improve his English. We talked about 2 hours during which time he told me about himself, his schooling, his family and other facts. He said that he was interested in Political Science and wanted me to explain some of the basic points concerning our American form of government. I told him that we would have to do this again when I returned from my leave.

        After he left I went to the Castle Terrace, and joined Bill Boun_ (OKED P10 man) for a couple of drinks. We talked for about 2 hours, and I doubt if I ever discussed so many different topics in many a week. Bill knows a lot of facts about OKED and it is always interesting to talk to him about what is going on. He also had spent some time in Turkey and so I welcomed what he had to say about Istanp Istanbul. Perhaps if I can get a ship from Haifa I might journey to Turkey for a visit.

APR 21

        Went to Character Guidance in the morning and managed to miss most of it by reading the St. Louis Post-Dispatch in the Men’s Room. The part that I heard wasn’t too bad, as they had a new Chaplin giving the talk. Returned to Kue and went to work where I finished a revision to one of my earlier estimates.

        The afternoon and evening was somewhat uneventful. I challenged the No. 7 man on the tennis ladder and got walloped 6-3, 6-0. The fellow just had too much experience for me and I usually made the mistake before I could get him to commit one.

        Around 4:30 I headed for Naha and the Kohuri Khan Theater. The theater was showing “Guys and Dolls” and the advance publicity was such that I couldn’t resist seeing the picture. Two and ½ hours later I walked out, and I can’t admit that I thought too much for the picture. Oh, it was entertaining, but too long, and the songs aren’t outstanding. I am looking forward to seeing Oklahoma and South Pacific in the near future, for they have some of the best songs that I have ever heard.

APR 22 (SUNDAY - WEEK 70)

        Looked as if it was going to pour down rain all morning, and consequently I thought it would be a good idea to go to Sukiran and see if they have any good travel books about Japan. Arrived an hour early, so got a much needed haircut, plus spent a while finishing off this weeks Time magazine. Didn’t find much at the library, but did read a couple interesting Fortune magazines. Have to admit that when I read this magazine the “Cash McCall”, “Man in the Gray Flannel Suit” or “Materialistic Charlie” throbs in my views. There were a couple interesting stories in the 2 issues that I read; one of them on Operations Research.

        In the afternoon Lichius and I road rode and walked to Nakagusuku Castle located about 2 miles from Fatemna. The weather had turned warm, but umid, and so we sweated quite a bit while walking to and from the Castle – or I should say the remains of the Castle. The building dates back to 1454 when 10,000 Okinawans labored for their lord Gosa Maru. The castle was reportedly destroyed soon after its completion, and now only thick walls, a few archways, and much ruble remain on the hilltop.

        There were many Okinawans at the Castle, some on picnics, some taking pictures and many enjoying the rides at the amusement park located adjacent to the Castle grounds. Must admit that this castle doesn’t compare to the Red Fort or Agra Fort, however, it is the best little Okinawa can offer.

Route as of April 22nd, 1956 – end of Chapter 11.

CHAPTER 12 - FORMOSAN FORAY, JAPANESE JAUNT

April 23rd, 1956 - May 30th, 1956

APR 23

        Took my time getting up and gulping down my breakfast. Around 9, Moe came to the hut and said that my plane was to leave at 1:40 and that I should be at the airport at 11:30 (typical 2 hr-wait). I did just that, and boarded the C-54 around 2 PM, bound for Taiwan.

        The flight was uneventful, and I spent the time reading and half-sleeping. Around 4:40 we lowered our wheels and landed at Taipei Airport. Took an hour to get the bags and be on our way to the city. I decided to stay at an Army hostel tonight and look up Joe Alfonsi in the morning. The hostel wasn’t bad, and the rooms and meals better than I anticipated. There are many G.I’s living in the hostel as I do not think there are any barracks in the city of Taipei – that is, for Americans.

        After dinner I walked around, and up and down side streets. The hustle and bustle was typical of the Chinese people that I have seen in Bangkok and Hong Kong. Many of the little shops and stalls were still open at 9 o’clock in the evening, and people were eating at little restaurants, buying food and goods or just walking around.

        Couldn’t see much of the city as it was too dark. There were the numerous bars near the MAAG compound, and I stopped in a couple of them to see what they were alike. Both of the places had many bar-girls and they would talk to you if you bought them a glass of tea (about $.60). I feigned being broke and sat and talked to the bartenders and a couple of girls who didn’t care if I bought them any tea or not. The dresses were a mixture of American and Chinese, and I will readily admit that there is nothing like the Chinese slit skirt, with the bare leg showing.

APR 24

        Got up around 7 AM, ate, and walked to the MAAG compound located near the hostel where I stayed last night. Didn’t get much information here so I decided to head for the CAT office since my prime reason for coming to Taipei (2 spellings) was to get my airplane ticket. At the sales office I got the information that I needed and consequently headed for the OKED Taiwan Area Office.

        Joe Alfonsi was out when I got there and so I waited until he came back from the Sugar Bldg. He was surprised to see me, and said that I should have written that I was coming. We shot the breeze for awhile and then went back to the MAAG compound where I cashed in my travellers checks for US dollars. Then we dragged my belongings off at his house and had lunch.

        Joe’s house is Gov’t furnished (Gov’t pays the rent) and is really a luxurious house – relative to the Orient. It is modern, with Western plumbing, large living room, kitchenette, both 3 bedrooms and a servants quarters. It has furnished it in a simple but quite adequate manner. The meals are prepared by George, the cook, and are excellent. I can not wonder any more why Joe has put on so much weight in the first 6-10 months.

        After lunch we went to CAT and again requested how much New Taiwan dollars that I needed and if everything is all right. Things seemed OK so we went back to the office where I gave Gene Donaldson $360 for him to cash in for NT dollars. He was able to get an exchange of 39 - 1, which is higher than the 36 - 1 that MAAG gives and of course higher than the official rate of 24.78 - 1. Back to CAT and then the boom lowered, as they said I needed a certificate that I had resided on the island for at least 90 days. This was impossible to get without a falsehood so Joe and I went back to think what to do. (also, what to do with $14,000 NT) I said that I wanted to try Northwest and he said O.K. The lucky cloud was with me – plus a few misguided statements – and I was able to get my Taipei – Cairo ticket for about $354 which results in a saving of about $165. We both breathed a sigh of relief and headed back to his house.

        Had a fine supper and sat back to decided what to do in the evening. We decided to get a sulphur bath in a resort about 10 miles from Taipei. The baths are giving Japanese style and I must admit I feel a little funny with a naked woman washing me. Oh well, – “when in Taipei, …!”

        Taipei is not very exciting although the slit dresses help arouse my imagination every time I see them. Nothing, – nothing like the Chinese dress anywhere in the world that I have seen. The city is somewhat odd, with __y brick buildings dating back many years. One sees many brown uniformed Chinese soldiers and it is not easy to forget the ominous cloud that hangs over this country. Chaing has his statue and picture everywhere and I can’t help but wonder if he is any better than the Communists. I am sure the “bled” Taiwanese wonder also!

APR 25

        Up at 7 and the 3rd of 3 fine meals at Alfonsi’s palace. He drove me to the Airport and checked to see if I would be able to get on the manifest. When things looked O.K he took off for work amidst profuse thanks from me. He certainly went out of his way to help me and to show me the town.

        The flight took off around 10 and I was back at Camp Kue at 12:15. Cleaned up, straightened out my things and got squared away in good old hut 722. Played a little tennis, and saw part of a horrible movie to round out my day.

APR 26

        First day at work, and while I was ready to do a small job, there wasn’t anything for me to do. So I goofed around the office, wrote some letters, talked to others who weren’t doing anything and just passed the time.

        In the afternoon I borrowed Stavely’s jeep and went to Naha. Picked up an application blank for the Foreign Service Exam and checked on my passport. Still no word as yet from Washington concerning approval or disapproval. (it had better not be disapproval!) Argued some more with the Vice-Consul about getting my passport before I got discharged but no luck. He says there is a ruling that no permanent passports can be given to G.I’s, and thus I will have to wait until 31 May, – dust the luck.

        On the way back to Kue I stopped at Tuttle’s book shop and bought McKay’s Guide to the Far East. Also stopped in to wish Lyle good-bye. He leaves on the Sunday boat and should be out of the Army in 3 weeks. To say the least, he is quite happy.

        Saw a good movie in the evening “Rebel Without a Cause” starring the late James Dean. Stopped in the Top 3 Club, and then back to Kue and the sack.

APR 27

        One good thing, – that is, by being inducted in the Army on 31 May, each passing of a calendar month also means another passing of one of my 24 months in khaki. Thus, as the days tick off this month, my 23rd month in the Army is rapidly drawing to completion. Soon, it will be only 1 to go.

        Lyle called in the afternoon and said that he would be able to join me at the Kue Theater and later at the Castle Terrace for a final send off. The movie was a horrible Western, but we stuck it out until the end. (I wouldn’t have if he wasn’t with me). Then we walked up to the Castle Terrace and had a few drinks plus something to eat. Lyle was a little upset because his boat wasn’t going to come in until Sunday or Monday and this in turn would postpone his getting out of the Army until almost his ETS. Nevertheless, he would soon leave the Rock!

        I got some more booklets on Europe today and now have quite a collection of Japanese and European literature. I really haven’t done enough reading for my trip, and thus had better stop dissipating my time in the evenings. Did read a book about Middle East and learned something about that part of this troubled world.

APR 28

        Attended training in the morning, and it was one of the worst that I have been forced to sit through during my tour on the “Rock”. Four of the boys gave talks on psychological warfare and besides not knowing what they were talking about, they were dull speakers who had no interest in what they were doing. I fell asleep a couple of times, and took extended “10 minute” breaks to get through this ordeal.

        It drizzled in the afternoon and consequently I didn’t know whether capt. Broome was still interested in playing tennis. It wasn’t raining too hard at 4 PM so I journeyed down to the tennis courts where I found the Captain waiting. My game wasn’t up to his consequently he walked off with a 6-2, 6-2 victory and dropped me from 11th place to 15th place in the standings. I will see what I can do about my game after I return from my leave to Japan.

        Went to Naha in the evening and saw a lousy movie. Seems as if I have seen nothing but lousy movies lately. The only exception is, “Rebel Without a Cause” starring the late James Dean. The weather was lousy also and I got soaked. I sure hope today’s rain isn’t an indication of what is in store for me.

APR 29 (SUNDAY - WEEK 71)

        Rained all day today, which together with yesterday’s rain made for a miserable week-end. Didn’t do much in the morning and since I missed breakfast, I was waiting – quite anxiously – for lunch and the typical chicken meal.

        Around noon I called Kadena Air Base in an attempt to contact the Transient Barracks where Al Dore was supposed to be staying. I left my name and number and answered Al’s return call. Around 12:30 he called and it was good to hear his voice which sort of symbolized home and the people I knew before coming overseas. He said that they had arrived from Seoul at 5 in the morning and were to stay on “the Rock” until Tuesday morning. I told him to come to Kue and to bring his clothes and stay in Sam’s old room.

        Around 1:30 I met Al at the main gate and walked him back to the Hut. It was good to see him and we spent the next 3 hours talking of old things, his trip & things in general. His tour would be up in less than 2 months and to say the least, is quite happy to get out after 4 long years in the Air Force.

        In the evening I went to the new Sukiran Field House and heard the Air Force Concert. The music was delightful and quite refreshing and I and the other 5-6,000 thoroughly enjoyed ourselves. The program was quite varied and both classical, cowboy, spirituals, novelty etc. was included.

        After the concert we went to the Castle Terrace and had a couple drinks plus a sandwich. The Filipino singer and band were in fine form and it was a pleasure to hear their arrangements. Back to the hut, sprayed both rooms, and then hit the respective sacks.

APR 30

        In the morning I went to check out a jeep, but had to be satisfied with a driver and sedan. Spent the morning taking Al to Kadena where he got his things clothes from the barracks, went to Finance, and checked things at the new PX. Also stopped at the Plaza House where Al priced various foreign goods.

        Al went to Sukiran in the afternoon where the Band played before a packed house of around 10,000 Okinawan school children. There would be few opportunities for these kids to hear music of this nature, and I was glad to hear that one of these concerts was reserved for them.

        I went to work in the afternoon and finished off a revised estimate that had come back. It concerned the mooring facilities for the Jacona Power Plant. Also, read the morning mail & picked up the boat mail that came in the afternoon — consisted of 3 St. Louis Post Dispatches.

        In the evening I stayed in the hut and packed for the trip to Japan tomorrow. Also read the Posts and talked some more to Al. He told me about his plants for the future which consisted of going to Howard Summer School to study German and then to Columbia in the fall to work on his Masters and Doctors Degrees. He plans to get a degree in history and eventually teach it at some college. It was good to hear of his plans for America needs dedicated men such as him and others like him.

MAY 01

        I thought that I would catch my hop to Japan in the afternoon, but both planes were filled with persons with a higher priority, consequently, I remained on the “Rock” for a couple more days. The fellow at the Airport thought that I would get away on Thursday’s flight.

        Al was supposed to leave in the morning, so I went about trying to scrounge a ride or sedan. Finally borrowed Lewis’s sedan, and about 10:00 o’clock I took him to Kadena. We were just in time as the others were beginning to board the plane. His next stop was Taipei, and thus on to Hong Kong, Manila, Saigon, Cambodia, and Bangkok. I was glad that he was able to stay with me the 2 days, as I like Al, and think he is one of the “higher type” people that I know.

        Rain came down in bucket-fulls all afternoon, and in a way I was glad that I didn’t make the flight. The office had a party at the Castle Terrace at 4, so I journeyed up there to partake in the free food and drinks. I missed the last party, and had to make this one, and was glad that I did, for it was an enjoyable little party. The purpose of the party was to celebrate the reaching the 300 mark for outstanding modification actions; Mr. Hands then announced that the next party will be at 150.

MAY 02

        Went to work this morning and thought that I would be able to do some personal work. However, I was assigned an estimate and began work on it. Then Delmundo came in and asked me to join them in negotiations on the Kume J Site. The negotiations last from 10 AM until 5:15 and while it was time consuming, still I enjoyed the hassle.

        Can’t really say that Kokuba’s men are top notch, still it was fun arguing with them, and trying to parry their costs down. Reminds me of Job Evaluation back at Dow, and the “discussions” we use to get in. Thinking back in regard to todays negotiations, I find that I like this type of work, and perhaps Labor Relations is the type of work to get in to. True it is new, risking and perhaps ulcer forming, still it is constructive and challenging.

        Saw another lousy movie in the evening. Boy, – I have seen my share of poor movies lately.

MAY 03

        I sort of piddled around the day, expecting that I would have no trouble getting a hop to Japan. Worked in the morning and did a couple odd jobs. In the afternoon I stuck around the orderly room, and when I hadn’t been alerted by 1 PM I called Air Priorities. Just my luck – all the rifle match participants were on their way home and thus no space for those on leave. Oh well, maybe Sunday!

        Began spending some time on my travel plans and spent the afternoon – organized athletics – reading brochures that I have collected. Also, went down to the dispensary to get my shot record up to date. Luckily they said that I only needed a cholera shot and I was presented with same. Heres hoping it doesn’t leave any lousy after effects.

        Nothing much doing in the evening. Read, got a sandwich and hit the sack early for a change.

MAY 04

        Last day of the week – thank goodness. Worked on a couple revisions at work and in general passed the time trying to keep busy. Since I am anticipating going on leave they are reluctant to give me any major work to do since I will be absent. No sweat on my part – 

        Stopped by Military Personnel and asked them if my old travel orders were O.K. The men there got all excited and after saying no, called up the company to see if I have been on leave the last few days. Then they said that I had to get another leave approved and so I began the long process. Got the form, my section chiefs signature and the 1st sergeant’s “John Doe.” About an hour later the orderly room called and said that the form was wrong and another had to be made out. Such crap!

        In the afternoon, – before my new orders had been cut – I received word that I was alerted for a flight to Japan tomorrow at noon. Thus I didn’t need the new orders at all, just as I told the 1st Sgt that I wouldn’t. Oh well, one can’t fight it all the time. Sooo it looks as if I will finally get out of here tomorrow. Lets hope there isn’t a plane wreck after all this trouble.

MAY 05

        I thought that I would be able to get away around noon, but “no dice” when I got to the airport. It seems that my plane was delayed and that they would call me later on in the day if it came in. I dragged my junk back to Kue and took it easy most of the afternoon. Around 4:30 I called the airport and checked on the flight, and was told that I must have been mistaken for I wouldn’t be leaving until at least late Sunday afternoon.        By now the glitter of the trip had worn away and I was even thinking of not going. I dumped my stuff in the room and headed for the library. While talking to Mr. Sauer, the library phone rings, and it is Andy saying that they just called and I had 30 minutes to get to Operations, Kadena. Well, I dashed back to the hut, threw my stuff together, and got security to take me to the Airport. Checked in, waited around, and by 8:30 I was winging my Tokyo.

        One flight was a commercial plane – Northwest – and there was reclining seats plus a hot meal. The fine service took away some of the bad taste and I looked forward to my brief visit. One dark cloud was the warning of not many flights to Okinawa, – that is for leave priority – so I might leave sooner than I figured.

MAY 06 (SUNDAY - WEEK 72)

        Awakened to a lot of rain and decided to check at the Osaka Hotel for flight information, and then proceed to Nikko. At the hotel they couldn’t do a thing for me – I have to go to the airport – and so I walked to the train station.
